english.title: Assault appropriate person acting in exercise of power conferred by search and seizure warrant under s.352 POCA
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), assaulted **(..SPECIFY NAME..), a

(A)_[National Crime Agency officer, who was acting in the exercise of a power conferred by a search and seizure warrant issued for the purposes of a civil recovery investigation]_
(B)_[Financial Conduct Authority officer, who was acting in the exercise of a power conferred by a search and seizure warrant issued for the purposes of a civil recovery investigation]_
(C)_[member of the staff of the relevant Director, who was acting in the exercise of a power conferred by a search and seizure warrant issued for the purposes of a civil recovery investigation]_
(D)_[National Crime Agency officer, who was acting in the exercise of a power conferred by a search and seizure warrant issued for the purposes of a exploitation proceeds investigation]_

under section 352 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002
english.legislation: Contrary to section 356A(1) of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
assaults
appropriate person
acting in exercise of power conferred by search and seizure warrant under s352 POCA

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence applies to Northern Ireland also. However this offence wording and penalty ONLY apply to England and Wales.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions
None

Note: When section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force the reference to 6 months is to be read as a reference to 51 weeks.
